selected.hook_line: If this island has food and water, why can't you stay forever?
selected.viewer_expectation: Enough food and water should make long-term survival possible.
selected.visible_contradiction: A full rain barrel and fresh food sit beside a shelter ripped apart by a storm.
selected.frame_zero: Full water barrel, gathered food and a badly torn shelter are visible together on the beach.
selected.character_action: The captain checks the full barrel, looks at the broken shelter, then raises the spyglass toward the damage.
selected.reaction: He pauses, lifts one eyebrow and gives the shelter a doubtful look.
selected.activity: comparing secure supplies with sudden storm damage
selected.location: small camp on an uninhabited tropical beach after a storm
selected.topic_link: Having supplies does not remove dangers that can injure you, destroy shelter or cut off what you need.
selected.factual_anchor: Food and water can help survival, but storms, injury, illness and other dangers can still threaten a person over time.
selected.payoff: No. Food and water alone cannot make island life safe forever, and a normal human life still has limits.

entry_bridge.a_end: The captain steadies the spyglass toward the torn shelter and offers the eyepiece forward.
entry_bridge.b_start: A hand with a blue cuff holds the same spyglass, with the torn shelter visible through the lens.
entry_bridge.reveal: The lens follows the broken shelter to wind-bent palms and storm debris, showing that supplies are only part of survival.
entry_bridge.world_entry: Storm debris surrounds damaged shelter materials while stored food and water remain untouched nearby.

novelty.prop_family: full rain barrel and torn shelter
novelty.reveal_family: a secure camp can still be disrupted
